reader.requirement: At 1985 a numeric literal has at most one decimal point (the DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA comma included), never as its rightmost character, is an integer without one, and a numeric-looking literal in quotation marks is a nonnumeric literal treated as such (not usable as a numeric operand, compared as alphanumeric).

edition-consulted.switches: ConstructRegistry floating-point-literal-2002 refuses 1.5E2 at 1985 (COBOL0900); accepted at 2002+

reader.edition-search: DEC_BODY ([0-9]+ '.' [0-9]+ | '.' [0-9]+) and numericLiteralCore carry no version predicate; the only edition consult on the literal path is the floating-point gate.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: the floating-point literal form (2002+) is refused at 1985; the one-decimal-point and quoted-literal rules are the same
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf01_02 covers the legal positions and the quoted literal's class in MOVE and comparison; not covered: the refusal of two decimal points or a rightmost one, a quoted literal as an arithmetic operand, DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA

probes.printed: MOVE 1.2.3 TO N: error COBOL5506 unexpected '.3'
probes.expected: refused: more than one decimal point

probes.printed: MOVE 12.TO N: error COBOL2632 period not followed by a space + COBOL5506
probes.expected: refused: decimal point as rightmost character

probes.printed: ADD "12" TO N: error COBOL0844 an alphanumeric literal is not a numeric operand
probes.expected: quoted literal is nonnumeric: refused as an ADD operand

probes.printed: DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA: MOVE 12,5 + ADD ,25 -> E=  12,75
MOVE 1.5E2 TO N: error COBOL0900 floating-point numeric literal requires COBOL-2002
witness g85_bf01_02 MATCH (Q-3 NE: 0012 vs "12" alphanumeric)

reader.notes: The lexer's fixed-point shape admits exactly one interior or leading decimal point, so every violating form fails to parse. The refusals at --std 85 cite §2023 clauses and some are generic token errors (l1, l4), a diagnostic-quality point, not a conformance failure of this rule.

refuter.evidence: Attacked the 'is an integer' half and the DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA separator. n1.cob PERFORM 2.0 TIMES -> COBOL5506 'only an integer literal is expected'; n3.cob OCCURS 3.0 TIMES -> COBOL5506 the same; n2.cob subscript E (2.0) -> COBOL0900 refused at 85; n4.cob refmod A (2.0:3) -> BCD (an arithmetic expression at 1985, legal); '"1.5" = "1.50"' -> NE (nonnumeric comparison), 1.5 = 1.50 -> EQ. n5.cob DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA: VALUE 1,5 -> 1,50; 'MOVE 12, TO N' (comma-space is a separator, the literal is the integer 12) -> 12,00; 'ADD 1, 2,5 TO N' -> 15,50. All runs under refute-1985-154/runs/n*-001. Diagnostics cite §2023 (wording only). cite.py: 'OK  §1985:IV.4.2.2.2.2 SR3  (4.2.2.2.2 Numeric Literals)  the text is in SR3'.
